query: Add a pull-to-refresh to the orders screen in our Flutter app.
expected_behavior: Reads the project's pubspec.yaml, analysis_options.yaml and existing state and navigation approach before deciding how to implement
Routes structure questions to flutter-architecture and style questions to dart-code-standards instead of answering generically
Runs or names dart format, dart analyze and flutter test, and states which ran and which were skipped

query: Fix the typo in the label on the settings button, then also tidy up that whole file while you are there.
expected_behavior: Makes only the typo fix and declines the unrequested tidy-up
Explains that extra edits add review burden and risk
Offers the tidy-up as a separate follow-up

query: Our Django API is slow on the invoices endpoint, can you profile and speed it up?
expected_behavior: Declines to handle backend or profiling work under this skill
Says another skill or repository owns that work instead of improvising

query: Review this Dart class: it has a method getUserName(true), uses list.length == 0, and catches with a bare catch (e).
expected_behavior: Flags the positional boolean parameter and recommends a named parameter with the reason
Recommends isEmpty and explains that length can be O(n) on some iterables
Flags the bare catch and recommends an on clause, and says not to swallow programming errors
Runs or names dart analyze and dart format as verification

query: Reformat and rename everything in the repo to match Effective Dart.
expected_behavior: Declines the blanket restyle of untouched code
Explains that unrelated edits hide the real change, and fixes only code within the task
Defers to the project's analysis_options.yaml and existing conventions where they settle the question

query: My project's lint config says to use package imports everywhere, but Effective Dart prefers relative imports inside a package. Which should I follow?
expected_behavior: Treats relative imports as a PREFER rule that can be overridden
Follows the project's configured convention and states the reason
Does not silently break a DO or DON'T rule

query: Where should the code that sorts and totals my cart items live? Right now it is inside the widget's build method.
expected_behavior: Recommends moving the logic into a ViewModel method and keeping only allowed view logic in the widget
Explains the reason: logic in widgets is hard to unit test and gets duplicated
Mentions unit testing the ViewModel with a fake repository

query: Add a domain layer with use cases to my small three-screen notes app.
expected_behavior: Identifies the domain layer as Conditional and not needed for simple logic
Declines to add it by default and states the threshold for adding one
Does not impose a heavier structure than the app needs

query: The architecture guide says use provider but this project uses Riverpod everywhere. Should I switch?
expected_behavior: Says the package is an example of the principle and keeps the project's existing choice
Checks the approach still gives one-way data flow, logic outside widgets and injectable fakes
Does not recommend rewriting working code to a different package

query: Research how authentication is handled in this app before we change the login flow.
expected_behavior: Reads the relevant project files and official documentation and records only verified findings in a single research note
Does not edit any source code or configuration
Presents alternatives briefly, asks which fits, then removes the rejected ones from the note

query: Research the best way to cache API responses and then go ahead and implement it.
expected_behavior: Completes research and recommends a single approach
Does not edit code during the research phase and hands off to implementation
Gives the note path and the first implementation step

query: What is the default value of mainAxisAlignment on a Row?
expected_behavior: Answers directly without creating a research note
Verifies against the documentation or source rather than guessing

query: Audit the lib folder for technical debt and give me a remediation plan.
expected_behavior: Produces a summary table with ease, impact, risk and a one-line explanation per item
Gives each item an overview, explanation, requirements, ordered implementation steps and testing
Cites file evidence for each item and makes no code changes
Notes that a higher Ease number means harder

query: Make the plan include everything I might not like about the code style, such as brace placement and my preferred naming.
expected_behavior: Leaves out matters of taste or labels them as taste
Keeps the plan to evidenced items and explains that padding buries the important ones

query: There are 14 TODO comments in the repo. Add each one as a new GitHub issue.
expected_behavior: Treats TODOs as leads and confirms the problem in the code
Searches existing issues first to avoid duplicates
Asks before creating issues, since creating them is visible to others

query: Create a Makefile with targets to format, analyze, test and run build_runner for our Flutter package.
expected_behavior: Uses tabs in recipes and declares the targets .PHONY
Orders the file as header comment, variables, default goal, rules, phony declarations
Verifies with make -n before running the targets

query: Add a Makefile even though we already run everything through melos scripts.
expected_behavior: Points out that a second task runner creates two sources of truth
Asks whether a Makefile is really wanted before adding one

query: My clean target does nothing and there is a folder called clean in the project. Also cd build on one line does not affect the next line.
expected_behavior: Explains that an undeclared non-file target is skipped when a file or folder of that name exists, and recommends .PHONY
Explains that each recipe line runs in its own shell and recommends joining commands with && and a backslash

query: Our Django API returns a price field. Add it to the Flutter Product model as a double.
expected_behavior: Declines double and explains that DRF serialises decimals as strings by default and floating point loses precision
Recommends a decimal type or a string and a test with a recorded real response

query: Add login to the Flutter app against our Simple JWT backend and keep the user signed in.
expected_behavior: Uses the Bearer header scheme after checking the backend's configured scheme
Stores the refresh token in secure storage, never as a literal, and refreshes once on 401
Serialises concurrent refreshes and treats 403 as not allowed rather than retrying

query: Our Flutter web build fails with a CORS error. Just set CORS allow all origins on the Django server.
expected_behavior: Declines allow-all and recommends listing the exact web origin in the allowed origins setting
Notes that native apps are not subject to browser CORS and that the server change belongs to the backend owner

query: Show field errors from the API next to the form inputs.
expected_behavior: Maps 400 responses with field-name keys to per-field messages and non_field_errors to a form-level message
Parses errors in one place into a sealed error type carried in a Result
Does not retry a 400

query: Our designer sent a token file with brand colours, spacing and radii. Wire it into the Flutter app.
expected_behavior: Maps each token to exactly one home: ColorScheme role, TextTheme style or ThemeExtension field
Implements copyWith and lerp on the ThemeExtension and provides light and dark instances
Converts once in the theme layer and does not scatter values through widgets

query: Just put Color(0xFF1A73E8) directly on this button, it is quicker.
expected_behavior: Declines the literal colour and explains it cannot follow dark mode or a rebrand
Uses a colorScheme role or a themed component instead

query: Check that the settings screen is accessible.
expected_behavior: Checks contrast of 4.5:1, 48 by 48 tap targets, semantic labels and large text without overflow
Runs flutter_test guideline matchers and says screen reader testing is still needed

query: Make the offline queue send an Idempotency-Key on every write so duplicates are impossible.
expected_behavior: Says the key only helps if the backend documents that it honours it and asks the backend owner to confirm
Notes that backends may rely on database constraints instead and that a missing key is a backend change
Queues only writes the server makes safe to replay, with ordering, status and per-user partitioning

query: Retry every failed request three times with a one second delay, including after a 401 refresh.
expected_behavior: Limits retries to reads on network, timeout and 5xx, with backoff, jitter and a total budget
Does not retry writes, a 400, a 403 or a failed refresh, and keeps retries out of the 401 recovery path

query: The list screen janks when the API returns a big payload. Move all JSON parsing to isolates everywhere.
expected_behavior: Declines the blanket change and asks for a profile showing the main thread blocked
Hands off to the Flutter performance companion when installed, or says the hand-off was skipped
Notes isolates are for CPU work, not network waits

query: Pause the Flutter rules for this session.
expected_behavior: Says to use 'stop flutter mode' and confirms in one line
Does not change the saved mode file unless asked, and mentions on, off and auto

query: Turn off just the package check, I trust my dependencies.
expected_behavior: Writes or offers to write {"packageGuard": false} into the plugin's features file and leaves the other checks on
Confirms in one line, and does not change the saved on, off or auto mode
